title: Semantics stability prober for new embedding models and tenant-migration cadence
creator: Rowan Chen
description:
Goal: Create a repeatable, low-risk pipeline that (1) objectively compares candidate embedding models to production baselines across both semantic quality and system metrics, (2) produces per-tenant migration recommendations, and (3) automates staged rollouts with clear rollback triggers. This ticket implements the "Prober + Drift Window" pattern: a structured probe suite for semantics, a lightweight runtime profiler for latency/memory, and a migration cadence that prioritizes high-signal tenants first.

Scope and deliverables:
- Semantic Prober: a deterministic evaluation harness that runs against a stable anchor set (500–2k queries across domains) and computes: recall@1/5/10, average rank delta, top-k overlap, cosine similarity distribution shifts, and a signed quality score (weighted). Store probe outputs as timeseries for trend analysis.
- Lightweight Runtime Profiler: microbenchmarks across sequence length bins (short: 0–64, medium: 65–512, long: 513–2048), batch sizes (1, 8, 32, 128 where supported), and quantization profiles (fp16, int8, int4 suggestions). Produce p50/p90/p95 token/embedding latency, memory high-water mark, and cost-per-1M-embeddings estimate.
- KV/Cache Compatibility Check: validate that candidate supports our prefix/KV caching semantics (no KV eviction regressions), and measure cold/hot path latency delta.
- Rollout Orchestration: implement staged rollout policy via: shadow traffic -> 1% canary -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with per-step hold windows and automated rollback if quality or infra signals fail thresholds. Include per-tenant pinning: tenants previously pinned to a model remain pinned unless they opt into migration or pass acceptance gates.
- Acceptance Gates & Rollback Triggers: define pass/fail thresholds: quality_score_drop > 2.5% OR recall@5 drop > 3% OR KL divergence of similarity distribution > 0.12 => fail. Infra thresholds: p95 latency increase > 18% OR memory HWM > baseline + 12% => fail. Any fail during a hold window triggers immediate rollback and investigator alert.
- Gradual Deprecation Policy: 90-day deprecation window for older versions after full rollout, with automated tenant notifications and one-click tenant migration in Console. For tenants that cannot migrate, provide fallbacks to a smaller-quantized variant for a limited time.
- Telemetry & Dashboards: new dashboards for per-model: quality score time series, per-tenant delta histograms, p95/p99 latency, cost per million embeddings, and drift alerts. Integrate with existing SLI pipeline and add a regression-alert channel to oncall.
- Migration Tooling: CLI and Console action to preview per-tenant expected quality delta and cost delta, run a dry-run shadow comparison for a specific tenant, and schedule staged cutover windows.
- Test Plan: unit tests for prober analytics, e2e smoke tests (shadow comparisons, canary promotion/rollback), chaos test for mid-rollout infra failure, and sampling audit logs for semantic regressions.

Tradeoffs and decisions so far:
- We prioritize semantic stability over marginal latency wins. If a candidate reduces cost by >18% but drops recall@5 by >1.5%, we will require a rationale and PM signoff before approving broad rollout.
- Shadow traffic will use statistically-significant sample sizes to avoid noisy decisions; this increases cost of onboarding but reduces false positives.
- Per-tenant pinning adds operational complexity to the routing layer; initial implementation is a soft route in the gateway to avoid long migration work.

Open questions / risks:
- Anchor set representativeness: needs continuous curation and labeling across verticals; ownership required.
- Drift sensitivity: choosing KL thresholds affects false alarm rate; will iterate after 2 months of production probes.
- Quantization safety: some models behave unpredictably at int4; we will gate quantized production variants behind explicit perf tests.

Acceptance criteria:
- Prober runs end-to-end for a candidate model and produces a quality_score and runtime profile in < 6 hours for a full anchor set run.
- Dashboard shows model-vs-baseline deltas and exposes automated pass/fail for canary hold windows.
- Console exposes per-tenant preview and one-click migration for at least 3 tenants in pilot.
- Automated rollback performs within 2 minutes of trigger and preserves request ordering for in-flight embeddings.

Notes on implementation approach:
- Reuse existing eval infra where possible but add new probes as modular tasks to avoid coupling to large eval jobs.
- Store probe results in timeseries DB (existing metrics pipeline) with a compact schema to support long-term drift analysis.
- Implement rollout orchestration as a policy object in the routing service so the same policy can be reused for Dedicated/Private.

Expected timeline:
- Week 1–2: define anchor sets, implement prober and initial runtime profiler.
- Week 3: integrate probe outputs into dashboard and SLI pipeline.
- Week 4: pilot with internal tenant set (shadow -> 1% canary) and iterate thresholds.
- Week 5–6: extend migration tooling and per-tenant preview; prepare deprecation notices.
